theory.title: Future continuous for actions in progress in the future
theory.explanation: Use will be + verb-ing for an action that will be in progress at a particular future time, or to ask politely about someone's plans: This time next year, more people will be working from home.
theory.tip: Future continuous = will be + verbo en -ing.

content.passage: The city council has announced a ten-year plan for greener neighbourhoods. This time next year, workers will be building new cycle lanes and planting trees near schools. At the same time, volunteers will be collecting ideas from local residents. Many families will be using electric buses, and some homes will be producing their own energy. The council hopes that these changes will make the city healthier and easier to travel around.

items.prompt: Describe what your town will be doing in five years.
items.modelAnswer: I think communities can make a real difference when people work together. In my area, there are several ways to improve the environment, such as using public transport, reducing waste and supporting local projects. Although change can take time, small actions often lead to better results. If more people took part, the community would become cleaner and healthier. I hope that by the next few years we will have made further progress.
